intended_object: For morphisms f, g : A ⟶ B of commutative 𝒪_X-algebras (commutative monoids in X.Modules), the structure morphism 𝒪_X ⟶ E of the equalizer presheaf of algebras E(U) = {x ∈ Γ(A,U) : f x = g x}. On each open U it is the algebra map Γ(X,U) → E(U). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation, and its use in gluing the relative spectrum of the equalizer.
explanation: On each open U, the component is `algebraMap Γ(X,U) (equalizerSections f g U)`. Here `equalizerSections` is `AlgHom.equalizer` of the two induced Γ(X,U)-algebra maps on sections. So the component is exactly the unit map r ↦ r·1 of A, with its target cut down to the equalizer subalgebra. That map lands in the equalizer because algebra homomorphisms commute with the structure maps, as the docstring says. Naturality is derived from naturality of A's own structure map `A.toSectionsPresheaf`. This is the standard 𝒪_X-algebra structure on the equalizer subpresheaf of algebras. The setting (any scheme, any commutative algebra objects in X.Modules) is natural, and quasi-coherence is assumed only later in the file, where it is needed. Mathlib has no dedicated version of this construction; the definition is built from Mathlib's general tools (`AlgHom.equalizer`, `algebraMap`) and does not specialise anything Mathlib defines more generally.
